feed.title: HeatWatch
feed.subtitle: Where heat is breaking records, who it is reaching, what the rules are about to require, and what can be done about it.

entry.title: Weipa, Queensland, Australia, set an all-time station high of 40.4 °C on 19 November
entry.summary: The reading beat the town's November record of 39.9 °C set on 10 November. — Sources: Bureau of Meteorology, Weipa Aero daily weather observations, November 2026 · Bureau of Meteorology, Weipa Aero climate statistics (1992 to 2026), read 21 November 2026

entry.title: Heatwave warnings cover four Australian states and territories on 21 November, with Tiwi in the Northern Territory at Extreme
entry.summary: Severe warnings cover Sydney, the Illawarra and the South Coast of New South Wales to Sunday's peak, the Kimberley and North Interior of Western Australia, and the Peninsula district of Queensland. — Sources: Bureau of Meteorology heatwave warnings for New South Wales, Northern Territory, Western Australia and Queensland, issued 21 November 2026

entry.title: Birdsville and Urandangi in Queensland, Australia, reached 42.9 °C, the week's highest Australian readings
entry.summary: Fitzroy Crossing and Wyndham in Western Australia reached 42.6 °C, Marble Bar 42.4 °C and Ngukurr in the Northern Territory 42.1 °C between 14 and 20 November. — Sources: Bureau of Meteorology daily weather observations, 14 to 20 November 2026

entry.title: Australia's weekly El Niño ocean index fell for a second week, to +2.64 °C
entry.summary: The relative Niño3.4 index was +2.64 °C for 9 to 15 November, after +2.75 °C and a series high of +2.88 °C. The Indian Ocean Dipole rose to +0.80 °C. — Sources: Bureau of Meteorology, weekly relative Niño3.4 and Indian Ocean Dipole data files, read 21 November 2026 · Bureau of Meteorology climate driver update, 10 November 2026

entry.title: Murcia, Spain, reached 32.2 °C on 18 November, the latest 32 °C day on record for mainland Spain
entry.summary: The previous latest date was 16 November 2009 at Vélez-Málaga. — Sources: AEMET observations, as reported by The Olive Press, 19 November 2026

entry.title: The Philippines recorded a danger-level heat index of 42 °C at Mulanay, Quezon, on 18 November
entry.summary: PAGASA forecast heat indices of 42 to 43 °C for Puerto Princesa, Zamboanga, Iba, Aborlan and Borongan on 20 November, the danger band in a month that is usually cooler. — Sources: PAGASA heat index forecast, as reported by GMA News, 19 November 2026 · Regional disaster risk office CALABARZON, as reported by the Daily Tribune, 18 November 2026

entry.title: Rain over the Black Forest lifted the Rhine at Kaub, Germany, from 59 to 170 centimetres in six days
entry.summary: Kaub read 170 centimetres at 06:30 on 21 November. The rise came from the Upper Rhine, where Maxau rose from 339 to 507 centimetres under a continuous-rain warning that ran to 21 November. — Sources: Wasserstraßen- und Schifffahrtsverwaltung, Pegelonline gauges Kaub and Maxau, 15 to 21 November 2026 · Deutscher Wetterdienst continuous-rain warning for the Black Forest, as reported 18 November 2026

entry.title: Lake Kariba fell to 30.50 percent usable storage on 16 November, the reservoir behind Zambia and Zimbabwe's hydropower
entry.summary: The level was 479.82 metres and falling about 3 centimetres a day. On the same date in 2025 the lake held 7.68 percent. — Sources: Zambezi River Authority, lake levels, 16 November 2026

entry.title: Brazil's satellites counted 6,229 fire foci from 14 to 20 November, about 70 percent of them in the Amazon
entry.summary: Pará had the most, followed by Maranhão and Ceará. Daily counts ranged from 261 on 15 November to 1,681 on 19 November. — Sources: INPE daily fire foci, reference satellite, 14 to 20 November 2026

entry.title: A fire on the Beecroft Weapons Range in Shoalhaven, New South Wales, Australia, reached 410 hectares on 21 November
entry.summary: It is one of eight New South Wales fires at Advice level, alongside the H Pots fire near Cessnock at 101 hectares. No total fire ban was declared for 21 or 22 November. — Sources: NSW Rural Fire Service major incidents feed, 21 November 2026

entry.title: Western Australia issued bushfire advice for five Kimberley fires on 20 and 21 November
entry.summary: The fires are at the Mueller Ranges, Durack and Lake Argyle, the Ord River, Derby and Meda, and Stove Hill. A separate heatwave advice covers Drysdale River, Kalumburu and the Mitchell Plateau. — Sources: Department of Fire and Emergency Services Western Australia alert feed, 20 and 21 November 2026

entry.title: Indonesia counted 1,095 hotspots on 18 November, mostly in East Kalimantan, and Singapore's air stayed moderate
entry.summary: The count was 1,046 on 15 November and 425 on 17 November. Singapore's 24-hour PSI peaked at 79 on 14 November and read 33 to 52 on 21 November. — Sources: Indonesia Ministry of Forestry SiPongi hotspot counts, as reported by Databoks, 15 to 18 November 2026 · National Environment Agency Singapore PSI readings, 14 to 21 November 2026

entry.title: Queensland, Australia, has reported one person treated for heat stress on Cape York, and publishes no hospital series
entry.summary: Queensland Health reported the case for the week to 14 November. — Sources: ABC News, 14 November 2026, quoting Queensland Health · Watchers.news, 16 November 2026, on Northern Peninsula Area water restrictions

entry.title: Australia's work health and safety ministers approved new national provisions for extreme heat at work
entry.summary: Safe Work Australia will draft them under a National Strategic Plan on Climate Safe Work, starting with extreme heat, poor air quality and vector-borne disease. No timetable has been published. — Sources: OHS Reps (Victorian Trades Hall), 18 November 2026, quoting Safe Work Australia chief executive Marie Boland · Safe Work Australia, Best Practice Review of model WHS laws, final report, October 2026

entry.title: Queensland's mine safety regulator urged every site to review heat risks after a petroleum and gas worker was hospitalised
entry.summary: Resources Safety and Health Queensland issued the alert on 13 November after a worker was hospitalised with suspected dehydration. — Sources: Resources Safety and Health Queensland safety alert, 13 November 2026

entry.title: The COP31 cooling communiqué in Antalya, Türkiye, names the ILO first among partners for a heat resilience roadmap
entry.summary: Ministers welcomed a voluntary Global Heat Resilience and Sustainable Cooling Roadmap, to be tested during 2027 and presented in Addis Ababa. — Sources: Antalya Communiqué and annexes, Third Annual Cooling Ministerial, 16 November 2026 (Cool Coalition) · UNEP press release, 17 November 2026
